title: Compact Rights Matrix + Incident Replay Canvas for Workspace Admins
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a compact, scannable rights matrix combined with a time-based incident replay canvas for workspace and org admins. The goal is to let admins quickly answer: who had access to X at time Y, what changes were made leading up to an incident, and whether a rollout or policy change impacted cost or request latency. Target users are Workspace Admins and Security/Compliance reviewers. Key constraints: must fit into existing Console chrome, be performant in rendering large workspaces (10k+ principals), support export for audits, and align with access retention policies.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma prototype with two primary flows: (1) Rights Matrix quick-scan + permission drilldown, (2) Incident Replay canvas with event scrubber and correlated cost/latency charts

Prototype passes 5 moderated usability sessions with product/security stakeholders and achieves task completion for the three primary questions: identify current access, reconstruct access at a historical timestamp, and confirm rollback status
Design tokens and component specs documented for dev handoff (ARIA roles, keyboard nav, color contrast) and a minimal CSS/HTML sample for rendering the compact matrix
Export to CSV/JSON for audit logs and a permanent link pattern that can be referenced in incident reports

decisions: Use a compact matrix as default with hover-expansions for multi-permission principals to reduce vertical scroll
Incident Replay will be an event-ordered canvas (timeline) that joins permission-change events, role-rollout markers, and aggregated cost/latency series using synchronized scrubbing
Server-side pagination + client virtualization chosen to handle workspaces with >5k principals to keep initial paint under 200ms for common cases
Export artifacts will include a query fingerprint and signed metadata to satisfy compliance review without storing full export payloads longer than retention policy
